🔍 Data quality, diversity and fleets

Source: vignettes/articles/quality-diversity-fleets.Rmd
quality-diversity-fleets.Rmd
FAO34 <- fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Eastern Central")

🧪 Data quality

data_quality() shows two aspects of the statistics over time:

  • the share of the catch reported officially, and the share estimated (by the country or imputed by FAO), from the FAO status flags;
  • the share of the catch identified to species, genus, family, or only to a higher group such as “Marine fishes nei”, from the FAO taxonomic codes.
quality <- data_quality(FAO34$area_data)

A large estimated share in the latest years usually means that FAO has not yet received the national reports; these values are often revised in the next release. The country table shows, for the countries with the largest catch in the last five years, how much was estimated and how much identified to species:

show_table(quality$countries, digits = 1)
country country_en catch_last_5_years estimated_pct species_level_pct
Morocco Morocco 7,094,636.3 0.0 80.5
Mauritania Mauritania 3,371,495.3 58.6 76.0
Senegal Senegal 2,322,403.4 19.7 73.4
Nigeria Nigeria 2,207,354.6 41.1 32.7
Guinea Guinea 1,715,820.0 13.2 41.6
Ghana Ghana 1,668,263.9 3.9 84.9
Sierra Leone Sierra Leone 1,026,560.0 100.0 64.3
Cameroon Cameroon 990,473.0 100.0 45.4
Belize Belize 954,073.3 82.4 46.7
Georgia Georgia 635,110.0 100.0 37.5
Argument Meaning Default
top_n Number of countries in the country table 10

🌈 Diversity and concentration

diversity_concentration() computes, for each year:

Indicator Calculation
Number of species reported Items identified to species with catch
Number of countries Countries with catch
Shannon diversity H=−∑ipiln⁡piH = -\sum_i p_i \ln p_i, with pip_i the share of species item ii in the year’s catch
HHI of species / countries HHI=∑i(100pi)2\text{HHI} = \sum_i (100\,p_i)^2, from 0 to 10 000
Top-N share Share of the top_n largest species items or countries 
diversity <- diversity_concentration(FAO34$area_data, top_n = 5)
show_table(subset(diversity, Year %in% c(1970, 1990, 2010, max(Year))), digits = 2)
Year n_species n_countries shannon_species hhi_species hhi_countries top5_species_pct top5_countries_pct
1970 1,970 59 42 3.17 782.75 1,035.68 60.22 58.63
1990 1,990 93 44 3.00 1,085.65 2,066.01 60.17 77.37
2010 2,010 151 49 3.17 869.69 948.69 55.39 54.35
2024 2,024 358 40 3.74 495.43 1,238.71 41.71 66.04

Reading the indicators. A higher Shannon index means more species items and a more even catch; its maximum is ln⁡S\ln S for SS items. An HHI below 1 500 is usually read as unconcentrated, 1 500 to 2 500 as moderately and above 2 500 as highly concentrated. For example, three species with shares of 50%, 30% and 20% give H=1.03H = 1.03 and HHI=502+302+202=3800\text{HHI} = 50^2 + 30^2 + 20^2 = 3\,800.

The indicators use FAO species items, including “nei” groups. When FAO splits a “nei” group into species, Shannon diversity rises and HHI falls even if nothing changed at sea. Country indicators change when countries split, e.g. the USSR in 1991.

🏳️ Country groups

country_group_summary() sums the catch by groups of countries from the FAO country list: World Bank income group, continent or region.

income <- country_group_summary(FAO34$area_data, group = "income")
country_group_summary(FAO34$area_data, group = "region", top_n = 6, lang = "zh")
Argument Meaning Default
group "income", "continent" or "region" "income"
top_n Number of groups shown separately 8

🚢 Coastal countries and distant-water fleets

coastal_distant() splits the catch between countries that border the fishing area and distant-water fleets from elsewhere, and shows the main distant-water countries.

A country is coastal to an area if its land (including overseas territories) lies within 20 km of the FAO area boundary. Former countries such as the USSR take the coastline of their successor states. In area 34, for example, Spain and Portugal count as coastal because of the Canary Islands and Madeira.

fleets <- coastal_distant(FAO34$area_data)
show_table(fleets$table, digits = 0)
Fleet 1950s 1960s 1970s 1980s 1990s 2000s 2010s 2020s 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 share_2024_pct

Distant-water countries 44,466 445,371 1,504,436 1,350,301 1,139,483 1,001,035 870,407 592,420 602,407 600,205 626,229 551,550 581,712 11
Unknown 0 24 155,388 46,784 74,349 26,772 25,077 40,994 44,367 36,529 38,078 38,138 47,857 1
Argument Meaning Default
top_n Number of distant-water countries shown separately 8

The analysis works for marine areas; inland areas in the data are left out with a message.
